Name: AD
Documentation: **A measure of supply chain adaptability.** AD is an assessment used to understand how well a supply chain changes when conditions shift. Supply chain planners and managers create this measure when they review sourcing, production, and delivery options. Leaders rely on it to decide where to add flexibility or remove bottlenecks. A high score means the chain adjusts quickly to demand changes, supplier loss, or transport disruption. A low score means the chain is rigid and needs investment in alternate routes or inventory buffers. The model uses AD to compare adaptability across business units and to guide improvement work.

Name: AE
Documentation: **Overall asset efficiency score.** AE is the top-level indicator for the Asset Efficiency group. It gives a concise view of how well assets perform by summarising the rates of devaluation, rework required, and disposal. Asset managers use AE to track overall asset performance and to focus attention on the subordinate metrics that need action. The metric supports decisions on maintenance, replacement, and investment across the asset base.

Name: Asset Depreciation Ratio (AE22)
Documentation: **A measure of fixed asset depreciation.** This assessment shows the portion of gross fixed assets that has been depreciated. Supply chain managers and financial analysts use this ratio to understand how much of the original asset value is consumed. It supports decisions about asset replacement, maintenance budgeting, and capital investment planning. The ratio compares accumulated depreciation to the gross fixed asset value.

Name: CO
Documentation: **An assessment of supply chain costs.** It records the cost of activities and resources across planning, sourcing, making, delivering and enabling work. It is used to evaluate spending patterns, compare actual costs against budgets, and identify areas where expenses are concentrated. This assessment supports decisions about resource allocation and cost control.

Name: Capacity Utilization (AE32)
Documentation: **A measure of actual versus potential output.** Capacity Utilization records how much of an asset's available production capacity is used over a period. The assessment compares actual output to the maximum possible output under normal operating conditions. In the model, operations planners create this assessment to monitor loading levels, detect idle or overused equipment, and support decisions about scheduling, maintenance, and capacity expansion. It is grouped with Overall Equipment Efficiency as part of Total Equipment Efficiency Performance.

Name: Cash Conversion Cycle (AE1)
Documentation: **A measure of working capital efficiency.** It tracks the time from paying suppliers for inventory to collecting cash from customers. Finance and supply chain planners calculate this metric to assess liquidity and operational performance. Management relies on it to decide where to shorten cash cycles, adjust inventory levels, or change payment and collection terms. The value is influenced by planning, sourcing, making, delivering, and selling activities, so it serves as a cross-functional indicator of how well the supply chain converts resources into cash.

Name: Cost of Goods Sold (CO11)
Documentation: **A measure of direct production costs.** This assessment tracks the total cost of materials, labor, and overhead that go directly into making goods sold. Finance and supply chain leaders use it to evaluate profitability, set prices, and control manufacturing expenses. It is influenced by planning activities such as Plan Finance, Plan Source, Plan Make, and by sourcing and negotiation actions. Managers rely on this metric to monitor budget performance and identify opportunities to reduce cost of goods sold. The assessment supports decisions on production planning and supplier selection.

Name: DP
Documentation: **A measure of supply chain dependability.** It records how reliably orders are fulfilled as promised. Planners and sourcing teams use DP to assess whether current operations meet customer expectations and to identify where schedules or suppliers fall short. The assessment captures actual performance against agreed delivery or availability commitments, providing an evidence base for decisions on inventory, capacity, and supplier selection. It is created from operational data by those responsible for planning and fulfillment and is relied on by managers who approve corrective actions or investment in resilience.

Name: Days Payables Outstanding (AE13)
Documentation: **Time taken to pay suppliers.** This metric measures the average number of days an organisation takes to pay its trade payables. In the Open Supply Chain Model, finance and procurement teams use it to manage cash flow and supplier terms. It is influenced by sourcing and selling processes such as Negotiate, Sell on Standard Terms, Source-to-Replenish, Sell by Proposal, Source-to-Order, Sell Custom Solution, and Source-to-Engineering-Order. This metric supports decisions on payment scheduling, working capital optimisation, and supplier relationship management. It is one component of the Cash Conversion Cycle group, alongside Days Receivables Outstanding and Days of Inventory.

Name: Days Receivables Outstanding (AE11)
Documentation: **Time taken to collect receivables.** This metric measures the average number of days from invoicing to customer payment. In the Open Supply Chain Model, finance and sales teams use it to monitor credit and collections performance. It is influenced by delivery and invoicing processes such as Deliver-From-Stock, Invoice, Deliver-to-Order, and Deliver-To-Engineering-Order. This metric supports decisions on credit terms, collection efforts, and cash forecasting. It belongs to the Cash Conversion Cycle group, together with Days of Inventory and Days Payables Outstanding.

Name: Days of Finished Goods Inventory (AE123)
Documentation: **A measure of finished goods stock age.** This assessment tracks the number of days finished products remain in inventory before they are shipped or sold. Planners and inventory managers use it to understand how efficiently the organisation converts finished output into sales and to avoid overstocking or obsolescence. It is influenced by delivery planning, scheduling of make orders and resources, and transfer activities, which shape the flow of finished goods through the supply chain. The Days of Inventory group compares this measure with raw materials and work-in-process inventory to give a full picture of inventory performance.

Name: Days of Inventory (AE12)
Documentation: **Time inventory is held.** This metric measures the average number of days goods remain in inventory before being sold or used. In the Open Supply Chain Model, supply chain and finance teams use it to manage stock levels and cash tied up in inventory. It is influenced by planning processes including Plan Finance, Plan Supply Chain Operations, Plan Budgets, Plan Source, Plan Make, Plan Deliver, Plan Financial Forecast, Calculate Delivery Plan, Negotiate, Sell on Standard Terms, Source-to-Replenish, and Sell by Proposal. This metric supports decisions on inventory targets, production scheduling, and supplier lead times. It is part of the Cash Conversion Cycle group, alongside Days Receivables Outstanding and Days Payables Outstanding.

Name: Days of Raw Materials Inventory (AE121)
Documentation: **A measure of raw materials stock age.** This assessment records the number of days raw materials are held in inventory before being issued to production. Procurement and inventory teams use it to monitor supplier lead times, order quantities, and storage costs, ensuring that materials are available for manufacturing without tying up excess capital. In the Days of Inventory group, it provides the input-side view of inventory, complementing work-in-process and finished goods measures to support decisions about purchasing and stock levels.

Name: Days of WIP Inventory (AE122)
Documentation: **A measure of work-in-process stock age.** This assessment tracks the number of days that partially completed goods remain in production between raw material issue and completion. Production supervisors and schedulers use it to identify bottlenecks, improve throughput, and reduce lead times. It is influenced by scheduling, inspection, material and resource issuing, and production activities, which determine how quickly work moves through the manufacturing process. As part of the Days of Inventory group, it bridges raw materials and finished goods to reveal internal flow efficiency.

Name: Deliver Cycle Time (RS12)
Documentation: **A measure of delivery process time.** It quantifies the elapsed time from order creation to customer receipt, covering activities such as reserving inventory, scheduling transportation, picking, packing, loading, and shipping. Planners and delivery managers use this assessment to monitor performance, identify bottlenecks, and set realistic delivery promises. As part of Order Cycle Time, it isolates the delivery segment to support decisions that reduce overall lead time and improve customer service.

Name: Devalued Rate (AE3131)
Documentation: **A metric that tracks how much produced output loses value.** It records the proportion of items that are not sold at full value due to quality defects. Production and quality teams calculate this rate from inspection results. Managers use it to see where quality problems are hurting revenue and to decide where to focus improvement work. It supports decisions about process changes, supplier quality, and training. The rate is part of the Produced Quality group, alongside rework and disposal rates, giving a combined view of non-conforming output.

Name: Devalued Rate (AE331)
Documentation: **A measure of asset value loss.** This assessment tracks the proportion or extent to which assets lose value within a given period. It is used to evaluate how well the organisation maintains the worth of its physical and intangible assets. Operations and finance teams record devaluation events, while asset managers and executives rely on the metric to decide on maintenance, insurance, or disposal priorities. The metric supports comparisons over time and across asset categories to identify where value erosion is highest and to guide corrective action.

Name: Direct Labor Costs (CO112)
Documentation: **Measures direct labor cost in production.** This assessment quantifies the wages and benefits paid to employees who work directly on making products or delivering services. It is used by finance and operations managers to calculate total cost of goods sold, set product prices, and monitor labor efficiency. The measure is updated from production planning, scheduling, engineering, and material handling activities, providing a clear view of labor expenses tied to output.

Name: Direct Material Costs (CO111)
Documentation: **Measures direct material cost in production.** This assessment tracks the cost of raw materials and components consumed in manufacturing. It includes purchase prices, inbound freight, and handling expenses. Finance and sourcing teams use this measure to value inventory, control procurement costs, and support pricing decisions. The figure is influenced by sourcing plan calculations, purchase order creation, receiving, unloading, inspection, and supplier negotiation, reflecting the true cost of materials that become part of finished goods.

Name: Dispose Rate (AE3133)
Documentation: **A measure of how much produced output is thrown away.** It shows the share of items that fail quality checks so badly they are not used or sold. Quality inspectors record disposal events, and production supervisors track the rate to understand waste. The metric helps operations teams find the root causes of severe defects and reduce material losses. It is used in daily production reviews and quality improvement projects. Together with devalued and rework rates, it gives a complete picture of output that does not meet standard.

Name: Dispose Rate (AE333)
Documentation: **A measure of asset disposal activity.** This assessment records how many assets are disposed of relative to the total asset base during a period. Disposal includes scrapping, selling, or retiring assets that are no longer useful. Asset managers and operations teams supply disposal records, while finance and planning groups use the rate to understand asset turnover and replacement needs. The metric helps the organisation monitor whether assets are being retired at an expected pace and whether disposal practices align with efficiency and sustainability goals. It informs decisions about asset lifecycle management and capital allocation.

Name: Disposition Cycle Time (RS3)
Documentation: **A measure of disposition processing speed.** It tracks the time from when a product is designated for disposition, such as return, repair, recycle, or disposal, to when the disposition is completed. This metric helps supply chain managers monitor the efficiency of reverse logistics and returns management. It is influenced by the sell renewal process, which generates returned items, and the source returns process, which handles supplier returns. By reducing disposition cycle time, organizations can improve asset recovery and reduce holding costs.

Name: Distribution Costs (CO12)
Documentation: **Costs of moving and storing goods.** This assessment captures expenses for transporting products, warehousing, and handling inventory. Supply chain and logistics managers use it to manage delivery costs and optimize distribution networks. It is influenced by Plan Deliver, Plan Financial Forecast, and related processes like Sell on Standard Terms, Source-to-Replenish, and Receive. The metric helps evaluate carrier performance and choose cost-effective shipping modes. It supports decisions on warehouse locations and freight contracts.

Name: Duplicate Payments Ratio (AE134)
Documentation: **A measure of duplicate payment occurrence.** This assessment tracks the proportion of supplier invoice payments that are duplicates of previously paid invoices. Accounts payable and finance teams use the ratio to detect errors, fraud, or process weaknesses in the payment system. It supports internal controls and process improvement efforts to prevent overpayment and financial loss. A high duplicate payment ratio indicates a need for stronger verification procedures and system safeguards.

Name: Early Payments Ratio (AE131)
Documentation: **A measure of early payment frequency.** This assessment tracks the proportion of supplier invoices paid before the contractual due date. Accounts payable teams use the ratio to understand cash flow timing and the organization's adherence to payment terms. It supports decisions about discount capture, cash management, and supplier relationship strategies. The ratio helps identify opportunities for early payment discounts and potential inefficiencies in payment scheduling.

Name: Environmental Sustainability Ratio (SD1)
Documentation: **A measure of environmental efficiency.** Environmental Sustainability Ratio (SD1) expresses the relationship between an organisation's environmental impacts and a chosen business denominator, such as production volume or financial value. The metric is influenced by supply chain activities in sourcing, making, selling, and reporting, and it supports decisions by those responsible for managing sustainability and communicating performance. It provides a single indicator for comparing environmental efficiency across different periods or business units.

Name: Equipment Availability (AE311)
Documentation: **The share of planned production time equipment is available.** This assessment measures downtime losses for a piece of equipment. It is used as part of the Overall Equipment Efficiency assessment, alongside equipment performance and produced quality. Production operators and maintenance teams record availability data, and production managers rely on it to schedule maintenance, plan capacity, and evaluate equipment readiness. The result supports decisions about repairs, preventive actions, and resource allocation.

Name: Equipment Performance (AE312)
Documentation: **The speed at which equipment operates relative to ideal.** This assessment compares actual operating speed to the designed or expected speed, capturing performance losses such as slow cycles or minor stops. It is one component of the Overall Equipment Efficiency assessment, used with equipment availability and produced quality. Process engineers and production supervisors use this measure to identify underperforming equipment, adjust settings, and improve throughput without changing product quality.

Name: Error-free Documentation Ratio (DP15)
Documentation: **A measure of order documentation accuracy.** It tracks the proportion of orders accompanied by complete, correct, and error-free documents. Supply chain managers use this ratio to evaluate the performance of order capture, invoicing, and delivery documentation processes. A high value indicates that customers receive the paperwork they need without errors, supporting smooth order processing and payment. It is one component of the perfect order ratio.

Name: Finished Goods Inventory - Blocked (AE1233)
Documentation: **A measure of blocked finished goods inventory.** This assessment shows, in days of supply, the quantity of finished goods that is completely unavailable for customer orders or production use because of quality failures, safety concerns, or other blocking reasons. Supply chain and quality teams use this metric to monitor the amount of stock that does not generate revenue and requires scrapping or rework. It supports decisions on inventory write-offs, disposition, and process improvement to reduce the occurrence of blocked stock.

Name: Finished Goods Inventory - Restricted (AE1232)
Documentation: **A measure of restricted finished goods inventory.** This assessment quantifies, in days of supply, the portion of finished goods that is withheld from free sale or use due to quality issues, regulatory holds, or other constraints. Inventory and quality managers track this metric to see how much stock is tied up awaiting resolution of those restrictions. It supports decisions on rework, disposal, release processes, and working capital management, because restricted inventory ties up cash and warehouse space while not being available for normal customer demand.

Name: Finished Goods Inventory - Unrestricted (AE1231)
Documentation: **A measure of unrestricted finished goods inventory.** This assessment shows the number of days of demand the organisation covers using finished goods that are free of any quality, regulatory, or other holds. Inventory planners and supply chain managers create and review this metric to understand true available stock, separate from restricted or blocked quantities. It supports decisions on production scheduling, replenishment, and order promising, because unrestricted inventory is the only portion that is immediately usable to fulfil customer orders.

Name: Fixed Asset Turns (AE2)
Documentation: **A measure of capital productivity.** It shows how much revenue the organisation generates for each unit of fixed assets such as plant, property, and equipment. Finance and operations planners compute the ratio to evaluate whether investments in fixed assets are being used effectively. Leaders use the result to compare performance over time, prioritise capital spending, or identify underused facilities. The metric draws on planning and financial processes, so it connects asset investment decisions with supply chain planning outcomes.

Name: Fulfillment Cost (CO122)
Documentation: **Measures the cost to fulfill orders.** It aggregates the expenses of picking, packing, loading, shipping, and scheduling transportation and delivery. Supply chain managers use this assessment to track distribution expenses, compare performance across periods or channels, and identify opportunities to reduce cost without harming service. The metric supports decisions on warehouse layout, automation, carrier selection, and delivery scheduling. It is influenced by daily execution of the related operational activities and provides a financial view of fulfillment efficiency.

Name: Gross Fixed Assets (AE21)
Documentation: **The total original cost of fixed assets.** This metric represents the total original cost of fixed assets. Supply chain and finance professionals use this figure to calculate fixed asset turnover and depreciation ratios. It supports decisions about capital investment, asset replacement, and capacity planning. Gross fixed assets provide the baseline for measuring how efficiently an organisation uses its physical assets in supply chain operations.

Name: IQL-to-MQL Conversion Time (RS41)
Documentation: **A measure of lead progression speed.** IQL-to-MQL Conversion Time (RS41) records the elapsed time between a lead becoming an information-qualified lead (IQL) and becoming a marketing-qualified lead (MQL). Marketing and sales operations teams track this assessment to evaluate how quickly early-stage leads advance through qualification. Shorter intervals indicate faster lead nurturing and routing, while longer intervals reveal delays in follow-up, content engagement, or scoring thresholds. Decision makers use the metric to adjust qualification criteria, campaign workflows, or handoff timing between marketing and sales, improving overall lead conversion performance.

Name: Intake Sustainability Ratio (SD11)
Documentation: **A measure of the sustainability of inputs.** This ratio evaluates the environmental impact of materials, components, or services brought into the organization. Sustainability management and sourcing teams create this metric. It guides strategic sourcing, supplier identification, and negotiation to improve environmental performance. It supports reporting and communication to stakeholders and influences sourcing-related processes such as Source-to-Replenish, Source-to-Order, and Sell on Standard Terms.

Name: KR
Documentation: **A key risk assessment.** It records the principal uncertainties and exposures facing an organisation in its supply chain work, including their likelihood and potential impact. Risk owners and planners create and maintain the assessment to capture the risks that threaten planning, sourcing, making, and delivering activities. Supply chain decision-makers rely on the assessment to prioritise actions, allocate resources to mitigations, and monitor changes in risk exposure. The assessment supports periodic risk reviews and continuity planning, ensuring that the organisation acts on known threats before they disrupt operations.

Name: Late Payments Ratio (AE133)
Documentation: **A measure of late payment frequency.** This assessment tracks the proportion of supplier invoices paid after the contractual due date. Accounts payable and finance teams use the ratio to monitor the organization's payment discipline and potential impact on supplier relationships. It supports actions to reduce late payments, such as improving invoice processing or cash flow planning. A high late payment ratio signals process delays or cash constraints that require management attention.

Name: Late Receipts Ratio (AE112)
Documentation: **Shows the share of receipts arriving late.** This assessment measures the percentage of payments received after their due date compared to all receipts in a period. Accounts receivable teams calculate it to monitor collection effectiveness. Finance managers use the ratio to spot delays in customer payments and to adjust credit terms or collection efforts. It supports decisions on improving cash flow and reducing overdue balances. The metric is tracked alongside on-time and uncollectable ratios to give a full picture of receivables performance.

Name: Lead Conversion Ratio (DP3)
Documentation: **Measures how many leads become orders.** The Lead Conversion Ratio compares the number of qualified prospects who place a purchase order to the total number of qualified leads. Sales and demand planning teams use it to evaluate the effectiveness of lead generation and quotation processes. It indicates whether demand creation efforts translate into actual revenue. Planners rely on it to adjust forecasts and align capacity with expected orders. The metric supports decisions about marketing investment and sales follow-up.

Name: Lead Conversion Time (RS4)
Documentation: **A measure of sales lead processing time.** It records the duration from when a lead is identified to when it is converted into a customer order. Lead conversion time is used by sales and marketing teams to evaluate the effectiveness of the lead management process. A shorter conversion time indicates a more efficient sales pipeline. This metric helps organizations allocate resources to lead sources that convert quickly and improve the overall speed of revenue generation.

Name: Make Cycle Time (RS13)
Documentation: **A measure of production process time.** It quantifies the elapsed time from initiation of a production order to completed goods, including scheduling, issuing materials, producing, inspecting, packaging, and transferring. Production planners and manufacturing managers use this assessment to evaluate shop floor performance, identify inefficiencies, and meet order commitments. As part of Order Cycle Time, it isolates the make segment to support decisions that reduce manufacturing lead time and improve throughput.

Name: On-time Payments Ratio (AE132)
Documentation: **A measure of on-time payment performance.** This assessment tracks the proportion of supplier invoices paid exactly on the contractual due date. It is used by accounts payable and finance to evaluate the reliability of the payment process and compliance with agreed payment terms. The ratio informs decisions about process efficiency, supplier satisfaction, and cash flow forecasting. A high on-time payment ratio indicates a disciplined payment operation that honors commitments.

Name: On-time Receipts Ratio (AE111)
Documentation: **Proportion of receipts arriving on time.** This assessment measures the share of payments received by their due date relative to all receipts in a period. Accounts receivable teams compute it to gauge how well customers comply with payment terms. Finance leaders track this ratio to evaluate credit policy effectiveness and to forecast cash inflows. It provides a benchmark for comparing collection performance over time. The metric is used together with late and uncollectable ratios to understand overall receivables health and to guide improvements in billing and collection processes.

Name: On-time to Current Schedule Ratio (DP133)
Documentation: **An assessment of current schedule on-time performance.** This metric tracks the proportion of orders delivered by the latest agreed date, reflecting adjustments made after the original commitment. Supply chain managers use it to evaluate how well the organization executes its current plan and to highlight internal schedule adherence. It supports short-term adjustments, expediting decisions, and process control.

Name: On-time to Customer Request Ratio (DP131)
Documentation: **An assessment of customer request on-time performance.** This metric tracks the proportion of orders delivered by the date the customer originally requested. Supply chain managers use it to evaluate how well the organization meets customer expectations and to identify gaps in responsiveness. It supports decisions about capacity planning, lead times, and customer communication.

Name: On-time to Original Commit Ratio (DP132)
Documentation: **An assessment of original commit on-time performance.** This metric tracks the proportion of orders delivered by the date originally promised to the customer. Supply chain managers use it to evaluate reliability of commitments and the accuracy of promising processes. It informs improvements in order promising, production scheduling, and lead time management.

Name: Order Cycle Time (RS1)
Documentation: **A measure of order fulfillment speed.** Order Cycle Time (RS1) captures the elapsed time from customer order placement to delivery completion. Supply chain planners and operations managers use this assessment to evaluate responsiveness, identify bottlenecks, and set performance targets. It is influenced by planning activities (P Plan, Plan Make, Plan Deliver) and sourcing processes (S Source, Sell by Proposal) that determine how quickly orders are processed. This metric supports decisions to streamline workflows and improve customer service.

Name: Order Fill Rate (RS2)
Documentation: **A measure of order fulfillment completeness.** It calculates the proportion of customer orders that are filled completely from available inventory without backorders or delays. Order fill rate is a key indicator of inventory availability and customer service performance. Supply chain managers use it to balance inventory levels with demand and to evaluate the effectiveness of planning and delivery processes. It is influenced by planning activities that set inventory targets and by the deliver-from-stock process that executes order fulfillment.

Name: Order Management Automation Cost (CO1212)
Documentation: **Cost of automated order management systems.** This assessment measures expenses for software, hardware, and services that automate order entry, validation, routing, and tracking. It is used by IT and supply chain leaders to evaluate technology spend, plan upgrades, and justify automation investments. The metric isolates technology-related order management costs from human labor, helping organizations understand the total cost of automated order processing.

Name: Order Management Cost (CO121)
Documentation: **Measures the cost to manage orders.** It captures expenses from order inquiry, creation, inventory reservation, invoicing, returns, and renewals. Order management teams and finance use this assessment to understand the administrative burden of sales transactions, monitor cost per order, and find process improvements. It supports decisions on automation, staffing, and policies for order handling and after-sales service. Influenced by activities like processing inquiries, creating orders, and settling returns, this metric links operational workload to financial performance.

Name: Order Management GRC Cost (CO1214)
Documentation: **Governance, risk and compliance expenses for order management.** This assessment measures spending on activities that ensure order management follows internal policies, regulatory requirements, and risk management practices. Costs include audits, controls, training, and reporting. It is used by compliance officers, auditors, and supply chain managers to monitor risk exposure, allocate compliance resources, and demonstrate adherence. The metric separates oversight and risk-related costs from direct operational expenses.

Name: Order Management Labor Cost (CO1211)
Documentation: **Labor expenses for order management work.** This assessment captures the cost of employee time spent on order entry, processing, and coordination. It is used by finance and operations managers to track spend, compare against budget, and support decisions on staffing levels and process improvement. The metric provides a direct view of human resource investment in the order management function, enabling cost control and efficiency analysis.

Name: Order Management PP&E Cost (CO1213)
Documentation: **Property, plant and equipment costs for order management.** This assessment captures depreciation, maintenance, and lease expenses for facilities, equipment, and other physical assets that support order management activities. It is used by finance and operations managers to track capital-related costs, assess asset utilization, and support investment decisions. The metric distinguishes physical infrastructure costs from labor and technology, giving a complete picture of order management expenditure.

Name: Order Processing Delays (RS22)
Documentation: **A metric for order processing delays.** It records the time and frequency of delays between order creation and shipment. Supply chain planners and delivery managers use this assessment to identify bottlenecks and improve order fulfillment speed. The metric is influenced by the activities of deliver-from-stock, including creating orders, reserving inventory, scheduling transportation, picking, packing, loading, and shipping. It supports decisions on resource allocation, process changes, and customer communication. Order Fill Rate (RS2) tracks the ability to fill orders fully and on time.

Name: Orders Damage Free Ratio (DP11)
Documentation: **A measure of damage-free order delivery.** It tracks the proportion of orders delivered without any damage to the products or packaging. Logistics and quality teams use this ratio to assess the effectiveness of packaging, handling, and transportation processes. A high value shows that goods arrive in good condition, reducing returns and customer complaints. It is one component of the perfect order ratio.

Name: Orders Defect Free Ratio (DP12)
Documentation: **A measure of defect-free order fulfillment.** It tracks the proportion of orders containing products with no defects or quality issues. Quality control and production teams use this ratio to evaluate manufacturing, sourcing, and inspection performance. A high value indicates that customers receive items that meet specifications, minimizing rework and dissatisfaction. It is one component of the perfect order ratio.

Name: Orders In-full Ratio (DP14)
Documentation: **A measure of complete order fulfillment.** It tracks the proportion of orders shipped with all requested items and quantities. Inventory and order management teams use this ratio to evaluate the accuracy of inventory availability, picking, and packing. A high value indicates that customers receive everything they ordered, avoiding partial shipments and extra costs. It is one component of the perfect order ratio.

Name: Orders On-time Ratio (DP13)
Documentation: **A measure of on-time order delivery.** It tracks the proportion of orders delivered on or before the promised date. Planning and delivery teams use this ratio to assess the reliability of scheduling, production, and transportation. A high value shows that customers receive their orders when expected, supporting trust and repeat business. It is one component of the perfect order ratio.

Name: Other Operational Expenses (CO13)
Documentation: **All other supply chain operating costs.** This assessment measures operational expenses not included in cost of goods sold or distribution costs, such as administrative overhead, utilities, and equipment maintenance. Supply chain and finance managers use it to monitor total operating expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities. It is used alongside other cost metrics to provide a complete view of supply chain costs. This metric supports budgeting and cost allocation decisions, helping leaders compare actual spending to plans and adjust resource use.

Name: Output Sustainability Ratio (SD13)
Documentation: **A measure of the sustainability of outputs.** This ratio evaluates the environmental footprint of products or services delivered to customers. Sustainability management, production, and delivery teams create this metric. It assesses how sustainable the organization's offerings are over their lifecycle. It guides product design, manufacturing, and delivery decisions. It influences value streams such as Make-to-Stock, Deliver-to-Order, and their engineering-order variants. It supports reporting and communication to stakeholders.

Name: Overall Equipment Efficiency (AE31)
Documentation: **A combined measure of equipment effectiveness.** Overall Equipment Efficiency calculates the product of availability, performance, and quality rates to show how effectively a machine or line performs compared to its ideal. In the model, production managers and improvement teams use this assessment to identify hidden losses, prioritize maintenance and changeover reductions, and track the impact of improvement actions. It is grouped with Capacity Utilization under Total Equipment Efficiency Performance.

Name: Perfect Order Ratio (DP1)
Documentation: **Measures flawless order fulfilment performance.** The Perfect Order Ratio compares the number of orders delivered without any error – on time, complete, undamaged, and with correct documentation – against total orders. Supply chain planners and delivery managers use it to monitor reliability of the order-to-delivery cycle. A low ratio signals problems in planning, sourcing, making, or delivery processes that require correction. It supports decisions about where to improve coordination across the supply chain.

Name: Planned Downtime (AE3111)
Documentation: **A measure of scheduled equipment outages.** It is used to track the time equipment is intentionally unavailable for maintenance, inspection, or upgrades. Operations planners record planned downtime activities, while maintenance and production teams rely on the metric to schedule work and avoid conflicts with production commitments. The assessment supports decisions about capacity, service levels, and maintenance budgets by separating intentional stoppages from unexpected failures. In the Equipment Availability group it contrasts with unplanned downtime to show how much of the total lost time is controlled and predictable.

Name: Planning Frequency (RS11)
Documentation: **A measure of planning cadence.** This assessment tracks how frequently planning activities occur within the order cycle. It is used by supply chain planners and operations managers to evaluate the timing of demand forecasting, supply balancing, and plan publication. By comparing planning frequency against cycle time metrics like deliver, make, and sourcing, decision-makers identify bottlenecks and align planning intervals with operational realities. The metric supports adjustments to planning schedules to improve responsiveness and reduce order cycle delays. It informs whether planning is too infrequent or too frequent relative to operational needs.

Name: Produced Quality (AE313)
Documentation: **The proportion of output that meets quality standards.** This assessment measures quality losses, including defects and rework, in the production process. It is part of the Overall Equipment Efficiency assessment, together with equipment availability and equipment performance. Quality inspectors and production staff record defective units, and operations managers use the measure to reduce waste, target process improvements, and ensure that production output meets customer requirements.

Name: Profitability (PF)
Documentation: **A measure of financial return.** Profitability (PF) records the margin or return an organisation earns from its operations. It is used to assess whether supply chain work creates sufficient financial value. Finance and management teams create and review this assessment; planners and executives rely on it to decide where to adjust cost, price, or investment. The metric supports comparisons across products, customers, channels, or periods and informs decisions about continuing, expanding, or stopping activities.

Name: RS
Documentation: **An assessment of supply chain responsiveness.** It measures how quickly and flexibly the supply chain reacts to changes in customer demand or supply conditions. Planners and operations managers use the score to compare current performance against targets, identify bottlenecks, and prioritise improvements in planning, sourcing, making, and delivering. The assessment provides a single view of responsiveness for decision-making and performance reviews.

Name: Raw Material Inventory - Blocked (AE1213)
Documentation: **A measure of blocked raw material days.** This assessment quantifies the number of days of supply of raw materials that are blocked, meaning they cannot be used in production or other processes. Supply chain planners and inventory managers use this metric to monitor the level of unusable inventory. It supports decisions about inventory disposal, returns to suppliers, and adjustments to procurement plans to compensate for unavailable stock.

Name: Raw Material Inventory - Restricted (AE1212)
Documentation: **A measure of restricted raw material days.** This assessment quantifies the number of days of supply of raw materials that are restricted, meaning their use is limited by certain conditions. Inventory managers and quality teams use this metric to monitor inventory that is not fully available. It supports decisions about releasing restrictions, reworking materials, or adjusting production schedules to account for limited availability.

Name: Raw Material Inventory - Unrestricted (AE1211)
Documentation: **A measure of unrestricted raw material days.** This assessment quantifies the number of days of supply of raw materials that are unrestricted, meaning they are fully available for use in production. Supply chain planners and production schedulers use this metric to evaluate the amount of usable inventory on hand. It supports decisions about production planning, order fulfillment, and raw material replenishment, ensuring that sufficient stock is available to meet demand.

Name: Recovery Ratio (SD12)
Documentation: **A measure of material recovery.** This ratio quantifies the proportion of materials or products that are recovered, recycled, remanufactured, or reused after use or return. Sustainability management and operational teams create this metric. It supports circular economy practices and waste reduction. It influences decisions in make and deliver processes, including Make-to-Stock, Re-Make, and Deliver Returns. It is used for reporting and guiding continuous improvement in product design and returns handling.

Name: Reject Ratio (DP2)
Documentation: **Tracks defective items rejected during quality checks.** The Reject Ratio measures the proportion of received or produced items that fail inspection and are refused. Quality teams and sourcing managers use it to assess supplier performance or manufacturing yield. It informs decisions about corrective actions, supplier selection, or process adjustments. A rising reject ratio indicates a need for tighter quality controls or revised specifications. In the supply chain model, it helps pinpoint where defects enter the flow.

Name: Rework Required Rate (AE3132)
Documentation: **A metric that tracks output needing extra work.** It measures the proportion of produced items that do not pass inspection the first time and must be corrected before they are sold or used. Quality control staff identify rework needs during checks, and production planners use the rate to allocate labour and time for repairs. The metric supports decisions about process capability, training needs, and equipment maintenance. It is reviewed alongside devalued and disposal rates to understand overall quality performance and drive continuous improvement.

Name: Rework Required Rate (AE332)
Documentation: **A metric of assets needing rework.** The Rework Required Rate (AE332) measures the proportion of asset work or asset items that must be redone due to defects, errors, or failures. It sits within the Asset Efficiency group alongside Devalued Rate and Dispose Rate, providing a view of how well assets maintain their intended condition across the supply chain. Asset managers and operations teams create this assessment from quality and maintenance records. They rely on it to spot recurring problems, trigger corrective action, and decide when an asset is no longer cost-effective to repair. The rate supports continuous improvement by linking rework levels to asset performance and cost.

Name: SD
Documentation: **A measure of sustainable development performance.** The SD assessment records an organisation's sustainability outcomes against its own targets and expectations. It is created by the team responsible for managing sustainability and is used to inform decisions about improvements, resource allocation, and reporting. Business leaders rely on it to track progress and set priorities. It supports the work of Manage Sustainability by making current performance visible in a consistent way.

Name: Sourcing Cycle Time (RS14)
Documentation: **A measure of procurement process time.** It quantifies the elapsed time from identifying a sourcing need to receiving and putting away materials, including negotiating, scheduling, receiving, inspecting, and transferring. Procurement specialists and supply chain managers use this assessment to evaluate supplier responsiveness, manage inventory, and secure supply continuity. As part of Order Cycle Time, it isolates the sourcing segment to support decisions that reduce procurement lead time and improve material availability.

Name: Stock Out Ratio (RS21)
Documentation: **A measure of stockout frequency.** It records the proportion of order lines or units that cannot be filled because inventory is unavailable. Supply chain planners and inventory managers use this assessment to evaluate the effectiveness of delivery planning and demand forecasting. The metric is influenced by planning activities: planning deliver, planning financial forecasts, calculating delivery plans, publishing distribution plans, and analyzing delivery plan deviations. It supports decisions on safety stock, replenishment, and planning adjustments. Order Fill Rate (RS2) tracks the ability to fill orders completely.

Name: Supply Chain Costs (CO1)
Documentation: **A measure of total supply chain operating cost.** Supply Chain Costs (CO1) tracks the end-to-end expense of planning, sourcing, making, and delivering goods. Finance and supply chain management create this assessment to support budgeting, cost control, and financial planning. Decision makers use it to evaluate trade-offs among P Plan, Plan Source, Plan Make, Plan Deliver, and Source-to-Replenish activities. It provides visibility into how planning decisions and source-to-replenish execution affect overall cost. The assessment informs cost reduction, resource allocation, and performance management across the supply chain.

Name: Total Equipment Efficiency Performance (AE3)
Documentation: **A measure of production equipment effectiveness.** It indicates how well manufacturing equipment performs against its full potential, considering availability, performance, and quality. Production and maintenance teams track this metric to spot losses from downtime, slow cycles, or defects. Operations leaders use the score to target improvement efforts, schedule maintenance, and justify equipment upgrades. Although no direct planning influences are listed, it belongs to the asset efficiency group alongside other metrics that monitor how assets and working capital support overall supply chain performance.

Name: Uncollectable Receivables Ratio (AE113)
Documentation: **Share of uncollectable receivables.** This assessment measures the proportion of outstanding receivables that are written off as bad debt or deemed uncollectable during a period. Accounts receivable and finance teams calculate it to assess credit risk and the effectiveness of collection efforts. Management uses this ratio to decide on provisioning for doubtful accounts and to adjust credit policies for high-risk customers. It highlights losses from non-payment and supports actions to reduce future write-offs. The metric complements on-time and late receipt ratios to provide a complete view of receivables performance.

Name: Unplanned Downtime (AE3112)
Documentation: **A measure of unscheduled equipment stoppages.** It records time when equipment is unavailable due to breakdowns, failures, or other unexpected events. Maintenance teams capture each unplanned downtime event, and production managers use the metric to assess reliability, identify recurring failure causes, and allocate emergency repair resources. The assessment supports root-cause analysis and capital planning by highlighting equipment that frequently disrupts operations. Within Equipment Availability, this metric complements planned downtime to give a complete view of total downtime and the balance between controlled and uncontrolled losses.

Name: Utilization Rate (AE3122)
Documentation: **A measure of equipment productive time.** Utilization Rate assesses the proportion of available time that equipment is actively used for production. It is recorded as part of the Equipment Performance group and reviewed by operations and maintenance teams to identify idle capacity, balance workloads, and improve scheduling decisions.

Name: Utilization Rate (AE322)
Documentation: **A ratio of actual output to potential capacity.** It expresses how much of available capacity is being used. In the Capacity Utilization group, it allows managers to see whether resources are overused, underused, or balanced. Planners and analysts calculate it from production, service, or asset data. Executives and operational leaders use it to decide where to add or reduce capacity, and to evaluate efficiency. The assessment supports actions like load leveling, maintenance planning, and investment justification.

Name: Velocity (AE3121)
Documentation: **A measure of equipment processing speed.** Velocity tracks how quickly equipment completes its assigned work, expressed as a throughput or cycle time. It is assessed within the Equipment Performance group and used by production managers to compare actual speed against expected performance, spot slowdowns, and target bottlenecks for improvement.

Name: Velocity (AE321)
Documentation: **A measure of the speed of flow through a process.** It quantifies how quickly work, materials, or orders move through a defined part of the supply chain. In the Capacity Utilization group, it helps planners and managers assess whether capacity enables fast throughput or causes delays. Operations teams create it from transaction or movement data, and leadership uses it to identify bottlenecks, set improvement targets, and balance flow across steps. The assessment supports decisions about resource allocation and scheduling.

Name: Work-in-Process Inventory - Blocked (AE1223)
Documentation: **A metric for blocked work-in-process inventory.** It tracks the number of days that work-in-process items remain in a blocked status, meaning they cannot be used in further production or moved to finished goods. Inventory controllers and production planners create this assessment by comparing the value or quantity of blocked WIP against daily consumption. They use it to identify inventory that is stuck due to quality holds, missing information, or disposition decisions. The metric supports decisions about whether to dispose of blocked goods or resolve the blocking condition. It is influenced by the Dispose process, which removes blocked inventory from the system.

Name: Work-in-Process Inventory - Restricted (AE1222)
Documentation: **A metric for restricted work-in-process inventory.** It quantifies the days of supply held in restricted status, where items have a limited use or require special handling. Production and quality teams record this assessment to monitor inventory that is not yet released for full use but is not fully blocked. The metric helps them decide whether to inspect restricted stock, dispose of it, or create a work order to process it further. Planners rely on it to avoid excess holding costs and to schedule inspection or disposition activities. It is influenced by the Inspect, Dispose, and Create Work Order processes.

Name: Work-in-Process Inventory - Unrestricted (AE1221)
Documentation: **A metric for unrestricted work-in-process inventory.** It measures the number of days that work-in-process items remain in unrestricted status, meaning they are available for use in production without any holds. Operations managers and supply chain planners create this assessment to understand the normal pipeline of work-in-process. They use it to balance production flow, set target inventory levels, and detect bottlenecks. The metric supports decisions about production scheduling and release of work orders. It is part of the Days of WIP Inventory group, along with restricted and blocked measures.

Name: 3PL
Documentation: **A third-party logistics service provider.** A 3PL handles transportation, warehousing, and fulfillment activities on behalf of other organisations. In this model, the 3PL accesses booking requests, booking confirmations, and export documents to manage shipments. The 3PL uses these records to plan and execute logistics operations, ensuring goods move from origin to destination according to agreements. Shippers and buyers rely on the 3PL to deliver goods on time and to provide necessary documentation for export. The 3PL supports decisions about capacity, routing, and compliance by exchanging information with carriers and sellers.

Name: Buyer
Documentation: **The party that purchases goods or services.** A buyer represents the customer side in a supply chain transaction. In this model, the buyer creates purchase orders and accesses customer forecasts, product information, order confirmations, and service delivery records. The buyer uses these records to plan purchases, track order fulfillment, and verify that delivered services meet expectations. Sellers and logistics providers rely on the buyer's forecasts and orders to plan production and delivery. The buyer's decisions about what, when, and how much to purchase drive demand signals across the supply chain.

Name: Carrier
Documentation: **A transportation company that moves freight.** A carrier operates trucks, ships, aircraft, or rail equipment to transport goods between locations. In this model, the carrier accesses tenders, tender acceptances, booking confirmations, cancellations, bills of lading, and driver/equipment records. The carrier uses these records to accept shipment requests, schedule pickups and deliveries, assign equipment, and provide proof of shipment. Shippers, 3PLs, and buyers rely on the carrier to execute the physical movement of goods according to agreed terms. The carrier supports decisions about route planning, load consolidation, and service performance.

Name: Seller
Documentation: **A supplier that provides goods or services.** A seller is the party that fulfills purchase orders by delivering products or performing services. In this model, the seller receives purchase orders and provides product delivery and service delivery information. The seller uses these records to confirm order acceptance, schedule production or service execution, and track delivery progress. Buyers and logistics providers rely on the seller to fulfill orders accurately and on time. The seller's decisions about inventory allocation, production scheduling, and order fulfillment directly affect supply chain performance and customer satisfaction.

Name: Accepted Offer
Documentation: **An accepted supplier proposal.** The Accepted Offer records a supplier's agreement to terms, pricing, and conditions following a tender or negotiation. Procurement creates it after evaluating offers and before awarding a contract, and it is used by the sourcing team to confirm supplier commitment and proceed to contract signing. It ensures that the agreed commercial terms are documented and accessible for subsequent award and contracting activities.

Name: Accepted Solution
Documentation: **A solution selected for implementation.** The Accepted Solution captures the chosen approach to address a business need identified through analysis of competitive landscape and supply chain priorities. It is created by strategic planners after presenting and evaluating options, and it is relied upon by teams responsible for transferring the solution into operational use. This record supports the decision to proceed with a specific solution and guides subsequent planning and execution.

Name: Acknowledgment
Documentation: **A confirmation of received request.** The Acknowledgment records that an order, inquiry, or other request has been received and understood. It is created during selling and sourcing processes, such as sell on standard terms, source-to-replenish, sell by proposal, source-to-order, and others, to provide a formal response to the counterparty. This business object is used by customer service and procurement teams to confirm transaction details and initiate downstream fulfillment or planning.

Name: Advance Shipment Notice
Documentation: **A notice of goods being shipped.** The Advance Shipment Notice informs the receiving party of an upcoming delivery and its contents. It is created by shipping or fulfilment processes, including deliver-from-stock, ship, and receive activities, and is used by warehouse and receiving teams to prepare for inbound goods. This record supports accurate inventory tracking, reduces receiving discrepancies, and enables efficient planning of dock and labor resources.

Name: Agreed PT&C
Documentation: **Agreed pricing, terms, and conditions.** The Agreed PT&C records the commercial terms that have been negotiated and accepted by both parties before formal contract signing. It is created during the negotiate process and used in obtain signatures to ensure that the final contract reflects the agreed pricing, terms, and conditions. This object serves as a reference for legal and procurement teams to verify that the binding agreement matches what was negotiated.

Name: Approvals
Documentation: **A record of official sign-offs.** The Approvals object captures the formal authorization from designated stakeholders to proceed with a proposal, plan, or other decision. It is created in obtain approvals and submit proposal processes, and it is relied upon by decision-makers to confirm that all required reviews have been completed. This record ensures that only properly vetted proposals move forward and provides an audit trail of the approval chain.

Name: Approved Return Request
Documentation: **An authorized return request.** The Approved Return Request records that a customer or internal party is allowed to return goods or equipment. It is created in create return authorization, schedule renewal, and schedule transportation processes, and is used by logistics and service teams to manage the return flow. This object provides the necessary permissions and instructions for handling the return, including scheduling pickup and processing the returned items.

Name: Benchmark
Documentation: **A standard for comparing supply chain performance.** Benchmark records measured performance levels and targets from internal or external sources. The Benchmark Supply Chain and Develop Supply Chain Strategy processes create and access it to set improvement goals. Strategy planners rely on benchmarks to understand where the organisation stands relative to peers and to identify performance gaps. The record holds metrics, data sources, and comparison contexts, supporting decisions about capability priorities and resource allocation.

Name: Benchmark Data (External)
Documentation: **Performance data from external sources.** The Benchmark Data (External) collects supply chain performance metrics from outside the organization, such as industry reports or competitor analyses. It is accessed in benchmark supply chain to compare internal performance against market standards. This data is used by strategists to identify areas where the organization lags or leads, informing target setting and improvement initiatives.

Name: Benchmark Data (Internal)
Documentation: **Performance data from internal sources.** The Benchmark Data (Internal) holds the organization's own supply chain performance metrics, gathered from reports and operational systems. It is accessed in run, validate & distribute reports and benchmark supply chain to establish a baseline for comparison. This data allows the organization to track its performance over time, identify trends, and support internal benchmarking and continuous improvement.

Name: Best Practice
Documentation: **A proven method for supply chain work.** Best Practice holds a documented approach that has delivered superior results in a specific context. Analysts create and access it during process standardisation, capability identification, and network standardisation work. It supports proposals for action by giving decision-makers a reference point for how similar work is done well. The record describes the method, its conditions, and expected outcomes, enabling the organisation to adopt consistent and effective ways of working across planning, sourcing, making, and delivering.

Name: Bill of Lading
Documentation: **A legal shipping document.** The Bill of Lading serves as a receipt for goods, a contract of carriage, and a document of title. It is created in submit documents and is used by the carrier and the receiving party to confirm the shipment details, ownership, and terms of transport. This object is essential for customs clearance, freight payment, and resolving any disputes over the condition or quantity of goods delivered.

Name: Booking Confirmation
Documentation: **A carrier's acceptance of a booking.** The Booking Confirmation records that a carrier or 3PL has accepted a request for transport capacity. It is created in select carrier and used by the carrier and the shipper to confirm the agreed schedule, equipment, and terms. This object enables the logistics team to plan the shipment with certainty and provides a reference for any subsequent changes or cancellations.

Name: Booking Request
Documentation: **A request for transport capacity.** The Booking Request is sent to a carrier or 3PL to reserve space for a shipment. It is created in tender load and used by the 3PL to plan and allocate capacity. This object contains the necessary shipment details, such as origin, destination, weight, and timing, and initiates the process of securing transportation for goods.

Name: Business Plan
Documentation: **A strategic and operational plan.** The Business Plan outlines the organization's goals, strategies, and resource allocations for a specific period. It is accessed in align strategy, assist with inquiry, analyze business plan, receive inquiry, identify solution, segment supply chains, analyze competitive landscape, and transfer, providing a foundational reference for many decision-making processes. This object aligns supply chain activities with the overall business direction and helps prioritize initiatives.

Name: Business Rules
Documentation: **Rules that define how business operates.** The Business Rules capture the constraints, policies, and guidelines that govern supply chain processes. They are used across the model to enforce consistent behavior and decision-making. This object is created and maintained by process owners and is relied upon by operational teams to ensure that activities comply with organizational standards and regulatory requirements.

Name: Call-off Contract
Documentation: **An agreement for goods or services on demand.** A call-off contract sets out terms and conditions between a buyer and a supplier for a period of time, with quantities, prices, and delivery details agreed in advance. The buyer places individual call-off orders against this contract when needs arise, without renegotiating terms. In this model, procurement teams create call-off contracts during strategic sourcing and source-to-order work. Requestors and planners use them to order supplies quickly for replenishment and customer orders. They provide a reliable basis for managing ongoing supply commitments and controlling spend.

Name: Cancellation
Documentation: **A notice of termination.** The Cancellation records that a previously confirmed booking or order has been terminated by one of the parties. It is accessed in select carrier and by the carrier to adjust plans and release capacity. This object communicates the change and allows both parties to update their records, manage any penalties, and reallocate resources accordingly.

Name: Certificate of Analysis
Documentation: **A document confirming product quality compliance.** Certificate of Analysis records the results of tests performed on a product lot against agreed specifications. Inspection processes create the certificate after physical or analytical checks. Approve Payment processes rely on it to verify that received goods meet quality requirements before release of funds. The record holds batch information, test parameters, and results, providing objective evidence that the product is fit for use. It supports acceptance decisions in sourcing and delivery.

Name: Channels
Documentation: **Routes to market.** The Channels object describes the various ways the organization reaches its customers, such as direct sales, distributors, or e-commerce. It is accessed in analyze business plan, receive inquiry, discover supply chains, and route inquiry to determine the appropriate path for customer interactions and order fulfillment. This object helps align supply chain capabilities with the chosen go-to-market strategy.

Name: Commodity Profile
Documentation: **A profile of a commodity.** The Commodity Profile consolidates information about a particular commodity, including specifications, supply market dynamics, and cost drivers. It is accessed in identify requirements, analyze supply market, and develop strategy to inform sourcing decisions and category management. This object enables procurement to understand the commodity's characteristics and risks, supporting more effective supplier selection and negotiation.

Name: Confirmation
Documentation: **A confirmation of order terms.** The Confirmation records that the seller has accepted a customer's order and confirms the terms, including price, quantity, and delivery date. It is accessed in sell on standard terms and source-to-replenish processes to provide a binding order acknowledgment to the buyer. This object serves as the basis for subsequent fulfillment activities and helps prevent misunderstandings.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **A legally binding agreement.** The Contract formalizes the obligations and rights of the parties involved in a supply chain transaction. It is accessed in deliver, contract standard terms, deliver-from-stock, deliver-to-order, obtain signatures, award contract, contract by proposal, contract custom solution, deliver-to-engineering-order, and contract renewal processes. This object provides the legal foundation for performance, payment, and dispute resolution, and is relied upon by legal, procurement, and sales teams.

Name: Corrective Actions
Documentation: **Actions taken to correct issues.** The Corrective Actions object records specific steps to address identified problems or non-conformances in supply chain processes. It is accessed in develop supply chain plan and publish supply chain plan to ensure that improvement measures are incorporated into future plans. This object enables the organization to track remediation efforts and prevent recurrence of issues.

Name: Credit Note
Documentation: **A document reducing a customer's debt.** The Credit Note records an amount owed back to the customer due to returns, overpayments, or agreed adjustments. It is accessed in deliver returns, sell renewal, source returns, review feedback, transfer, and receive settlement processes to adjust accounts and settle balances. This object is used by finance and customer service to issue refunds or credits against future invoices.

Name: Customer Forecast
Documentation: **A projection of future customer demand.** It holds the expected quantities and timing of customer orders over a planning horizon. Created by buyers or demand planners, it supports the P Plan process to balance supply and demand. The Buyer accesses it to align purchasing or sales forecasts with actual customer expectations.

Name: Customer Purchase Order
Documentation: **A formal customer request to purchase.** It records the items, quantities, prices, and delivery terms agreed with a customer. Created by the customer or sales team, it is used by order creation processes such as Create Order and Validate & Create Order, and by Release Contract to initiate fulfillment.

Name: Customer Segments
Documentation: **A classification of customer groups.** It holds definitions and characteristics that group customers by similar needs, behaviors, or value. Created by marketing or planning, it is accessed by Analyze Business Plan, Receive Inquiry, Discover Supply Chains, and Route Inquiry to tailor service and routing decisions.

Name: Deliver Supply
Documentation: **A record of supply available for delivery.** It holds data about inventory levels, incoming supply, and allocation status. Created by planning or execution, it is accessed by Gather Inventory & Supply and Calculate Delivery Plan to determine what can be delivered to meet demand.

Name: Delivery Demand
Documentation: **A record of delivery requirements.** It holds the demand for delivery, including customer orders, shipment requests, and required dates. Created by order intake or planning, it is accessed by Gather Delivery Demand and Calculate Delivery Plan to consolidate delivery needs.

Name: Delivery Plan
Documentation: **A plan for executing deliveries.** It holds the details of how outbound deliveries will be carried out, including timing, routes, and resources. Created by planning, it is accessed by Publish Distribution Plan to communicate the plan, and by Gather Sourcing Demand to align sourcing with delivery needs.

Name: Delivery Schedule
Documentation: **A schedule of delivery events.** It holds the specific dates, times, and locations for shipments and receipts. Created by planning or execution, it is accessed by multiple processes including Deliver-to-Order, Deliver-From-Stock, Receive, Inspect, and Plan Financial Forecast to coordinate delivery operations.

Name: Delivery Slot
Documentation: **A reserved time window for a delivery.** It holds the allocated date and time at a specific location for a shipment to be received or picked up. Created by scheduling or booking, it is used to coordinate arrival and avoid congestion at facilities.

Name: Demand Forecast
Documentation: **A projection of future customer demand.** Demand Forecast records expected quantities and timing of customer orders for products or services. Planning processes gather and validate the forecast to align supply chain operations, finance, and budgets. It is accessed when balancing supply and demand, ensuring that production, sourcing, and delivery resources match anticipated requirements. Planners create the forecast from historical data, market signals, and customer inputs, and it serves as a basis for operational and financial planning decisions across the organisation.

Name: Distribution Plan
Documentation: **A plan for distributing goods across the network.** It holds the allocation of inventory to distribution centers, transportation modes, and timing to meet demand. Created by planning, it is accessed by Plan Deliver, Plan Source, Plan Make, Plan Finance, P Plan, D Deliver, and Calculate Delivery Plan to coordinate network-wide distribution.

Name: Documents
Documentation: **A collection of business documents.** It holds various records that support supply chain transactions, such as certificates, instructions, or compliance papers. Created by different parties, it is accessed by Submit Documents to provide required paperwork for shipping, customs, or quality.

Name: Driver/Equipment
Documentation: **A record of transport resources.** Driver/Equipment holds information about drivers and vehicles used for moving goods. The Carrier process creates and maintains this record to manage available transport capacity. Assign Driver accesses it to match specific drivers and equipment to shipments. The record includes driver qualifications, vehicle specifications, and availability status, enabling efficient utilisation of transport assets and compliance with operational requirements in delivery operations.

Name: End-of-Use Return Request
Documentation: **A request to return a used product.** It holds information about the product, condition, and reason for return. Created by a customer or end user, it is accessed by Deliver Returns to process the return, Sell Renewal to manage renewal, and Source Returns to handle reverse logistics.

Name: Exceptions
Documentation: **A record of operational deviations.** It holds information about issues that arise during execution, such as shortages, quality problems, or delays. Created by execution processes, it is accessed by Issue/Stage Materials, Create Schedule, Produce, Inspect, and Package to flag and resolve exceptions.

Name: Execution Data
Documentation: **A record of actual execution data.** It holds information about completed activities, such as orders shipped, production output, and sourcing transactions. Created by operational systems, it is accessed by D Deliver, P Plan, M Make, and S Source to monitor performance and inform planning.

Name: Export Documents
Documentation: **A set of documents required for export.** It holds paperwork such as export declarations, certificates of origin, and shipping instructions. Created by exporters or logistics, it is accessed by Submit Documents to provide the required documents, and by 3PL to handle export clearance and transportation.

Name: Feedback
Documentation: **A record of stakeholder feedback.** It holds comments, ratings, and suggestions from customers, suppliers, or internal users. Created by stakeholders, it is accessed by strategic processes like Develop Supply Chain Strategy, Align Network, Define Network Solutions, and others to incorporate input into planning and improvement.

Name: Forecast
Documentation: **A projection of future requirements.** Forecast records estimated future demand, supply needs, or resource requirements used for planning. Plan Budgets and Plan Source processes access this record to develop financial and sourcing plans. Planners create the forecast based on historical trends, market conditions, and business objectives. It holds expected volumes, periods, and assumptions, allowing the organisation to anticipate needs and allocate resources accordingly. The forecast is essential for proactive decision-making in budgeting and procurement.

Name: Generic Stock
Documentation: **A record of unallocated inventory.** It holds information about stock that is available for general use, not reserved for a specific customer order. Created by production or replenishment, it is accessed by Put Away, Pick, Make-to-Stock, Deliver-From-Stock, Transfer, Sell on Standard Terms, Source-to-Replenish, Unload, and Inspect to manage stock movements.

Name: Geographic Map
Documentation: **A spatial representation of geographic locations.** It holds maps and coordinates for supply chain nodes, transportation routes, and customer locations. Created by network design, it is accessed by Define Supply Chain Network, Assign, Investigate, Determine Action, Perform Network Organizational Analysis, Analyze Network Standardization, and others to analyze and optimize the network.

Name: Goals
Documentation: **A record of organizational objectives.** It holds targets, key results, and performance metrics that guide supply chain decisions. Created by leadership, it is accessed by Align Strategy, Assist with Inquiry, Align Network, Assist with Claim, Tax Accounting, Align Processes, Assist with Custom Solution, Align Resources, and Assist with Advisory to ensure alignment.

Name: Gross Material Requirements
Documentation: **A calculation of total material needs.** It holds the quantities of raw materials, components, or services required to meet production and delivery plans before subtracting existing inventory. Created by planning, it is accessed by Gather Sourcing Demand and Calculate Sourcing Plan to determine sourcing requirements.

Name: Inquiry
Documentation: **A request for information or assistance.** It holds the details of a question or issue raised by a customer, supplier, or other stakeholder. Created by the inquirer, it is accessed by processes like Inquire, Assist with Inquiry, Initiate Renewal, and Process Return Inquiry to provide responses and route the inquiry.

Name: Invoice
Documentation: **A request for payment for goods or services.** It holds the amounts owed, payment terms, and related transaction details. Created by the seller, it is accessed by Sell on Standard Terms, Source-to-Replenish, Sell by Proposal, Source-to-Order, Sell Custom Solution, Source-to-Engineering-Order, Deliver-From-Stock, Invoice, and Approve Payment to manage billing and payment.

Name: Loads
Documentation: **A record of goods assembled for transport.** Loads holds details of goods consolidated for a single shipment, including quantities, weights, and destinations. The Tender Load process accesses this record to offer the load to carriers for transportation. Logistics or shipping personnel create the load when preparing goods for delivery. The record supports efficient use of transport capacity and enables accurate tendering and tracking of shipments throughout the delivery process.

Name: MRP Rerun Request
Documentation: **A request to rerun material planning.** It records the need to regenerate the materials requirements plan after changes in demand, supply, or planning parameters. Planners create this record when they gather sourcing demand or publish a sourcing plan, and the MRP system uses it to trigger a fresh calculation of net material requirements. It supports timely and accurate replenishment decisions by ensuring the plan reflects current conditions.

Name: Markets
Documentation: **Information about markets served.** This record describes customer segments, demand patterns, and competitive conditions in geographic or product markets. Planners and strategists create and maintain this data to analyze business plans, respond to customer inquiries, and identify strategic supply chain capabilities. It supports decisions about where to operate, which customers to serve, and how to align supply chain resources with market opportunities.

Name: Material
Documentation: **A record of a material.** This object holds identifying and descriptive information about a material, including its specifications, classification, and source. It is used in sourcing and making processes where materials are procured or transformed into finished goods. Sourcing and production teams rely on this record to plan purchases, manage inventory, and ensure the right materials are available for manufacturing.

Name: Material Requisition
Documentation: **A request to issue or move materials.** This record authorizes the release of materials from inventory for production, transfer between locations, or packaging. Warehouse and production staff create and use material requisitions to ensure the right materials are available at the right place and time. The requisition supports efficient inventory control and accurate tracking of material consumption across the supply chain.

Name: Materials Requirements Plan
Documentation: **A plan of materials needed over time.** This record specifies the quantities and timing of materials required to support production, sourcing, and budget plans. Planners create it during planning activities to coordinate the supply of components with demand. It is used to generate purchase orders, production schedules, and inventory deployments. The plan ensures that materials are available when needed while minimizing excess inventory.
